claim.summary: Published (Turan 1984, Section 37, Theorem 37.1). Weak Lindelof hypothesis with constant A: there is delta < A such that zeta has fewer than A delta log tau0 zeros in the disk of radius delta about s0 = sigma0 + i tau0 whenever zeta has no zero in Re s > sigma0, |Im s - tau0| < log tau0, sigma0 >= 1/2 + 10 delta, tau0 large. If it holds with some A < 0.01 then N(alpha, T) < T^(2(1 - alpha) + 5 sqrt A) for 1/2 <= alpha <= 1 and T large.
claim.assessment: Statement read as page images from a supplied scan; the proof read only in its first two pages; not audited. The book adds, citing an earlier paper of its author, that the count holds unconditionally with A = 0.71 (a constant read from a small scan and uncertain) for all delta < 1/10, and with every A at sigma0 = 1.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: A local count of zeros at the edge of a zero-free rectangle, weaker than the Lindelof hypothesis, which is the kind of count the notebook's shell exclusion needs when the excluded zero is the rightmost in a window.
significance.next_action: Read the cited source for the unconditional constant and compare with the shell exclusion's requirement.

claim.summary: For each 0 < x < 1/2 there are mu, R1 = mu + 1/4 + x/2 and kappa > 0 such that for all large tau0: if |sum over y < n <= y' of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau0)| <= C y tau0^-1 log^A y for all tau0^2 <= y < y' <= 2y, and zeta has at most kappa log tau0 zeros in |s - (1 + mu + i tau0)| <= R1 (a disk in Re s >= 3/4 - x/2), then zeta(1 - x + i tau0) != 0.
claim.assessment: Conditional result with a complete proof from the two-radius lemma and an elementary growth bound for zeta. The premise on prime sums is unproved; it is compatible with the pole, and its relation to the zeros near the height is not read. The exception is a cluster of at least kappa log tau0 off-line zeros in one disk.

formalization.scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

significance.rationale: States for zeta itself the second half of the missing implication with its exact exception: square-root cancellation of prime sums at one height excludes every off-line zero at that height that is not in a dense off-line cluster.

claim.summary: For large tau0: if |sum over y < n <= y' of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau0)| <= C y tau0^-1 log^A y for all tau0^2 <= y < y' <= 2y and zeta(3/4 + i tau0) = 0, then with s0 = 4.125 + i tau0 and d <= 3.375 the least distance from s0 to a zero, more than 0.02 log tau0 zeros lie in d <= |s - s0| <= e^0.02 d, all with real part at least 0.625; the disk of radius 3.5 holds at most 19.65 log tau0 zeros.
claim.assessment: Conditional result with a complete proof and constants checked by a saved script. The premise on prime sums is unproved; the threshold height is unspecified and the count is below one zero for tau0 < e^50.

claim.summary: Published (Turan 1984, Theorem 36.1), under the Lindelof hypothesis: for 0 < delta < 1/4 (bound uncertain in the scan), 6 delta^2 log(3/delta) <= b <= 1, delta <= b/a <= 1/2, if |sum over N1 <= n <= N2 of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau0)| < c N log^10 N / tau0^b for tau0^a <= N <= N1 < N2 <= min(2N, tau0^(a(1+2 delta))), then zeta has no zero on sigma >= 1 - (b/a)(1 - 2 delta), t = tau0, for tau0 > c(delta).
claim.assessment: Statement and proof read as page images from a supplied scan; not audited. By the author's statement the Lindelof hypothesis is used at one point only, to bound by delta^3 log tau0 the zeros in a fixed box to the right of the line to which Turan's second main theorem is applied; the kernel lemma and a passage repeated from an earlier section were not read.
